name: Concept I: Laser sail (Starshot-class) — 0.046c capture
description: Beyond-target · ultralight sailcraft, not a 1 kg probe. 0.046c cruise with conditional photogravitational capture at Alpha Cen A on the ~95 yr A/B arrival scale (Heller & Hippke 2017). Literature benchmark with extremely favorable sail loading (~0.00086 g/m²); the 95 yr A/B arrival is not a solved A-only parking orbit. A highly reflective, enormous ultralight sail must survive close stellar encounters. Launch, A-only full-stop geometry and orbit settling are not modeled. Heller & Hippke (2017): ~95 yr A/B arrival scale. A-only capture and orbit settling require their own solution; this is not a simulated parking orbit. Proxima via A/B takes ~141 yr, not 95 yr. Numbers and sources: docs/analyses/nano-swarm.md. Illustrative already-accelerated departure coast at 1 AU, with Newtonian solar gravity and the specified cruise speed at infinity. The hyperbola has a = -mu_sun/v_inf² and perihelion at 1 AU; it encodes cruise energy, not a powered launch. No laser impulse or capture event is fabricated. The preview stops at 30 AU; it does not solve a target intercept, relativistic launch, or destination braking. The roughly 100 GW array and gram chip refer to Starshot shorthand; the capture study instead assumes ~100,000 m² for a 10 g payload, not the same meter-scale sailcraft.
